prompts.display_text: Pin a country with 500,000 or more Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: Pin a country with 500,000 or more Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.summary: At the end of 2025 seven countries had 500,000 or more Church members. The United States led with about 6.93 million, followed by Brazil and Mexico at about 1.57 million each, then the Philippines, Peru, Chile and Argentina.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: About 1.57 million members, just ahead of Mexico.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: About 1.57 million members.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: About 6.93 million members.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: About 905,000 members.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: About 506,000 members.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: About 624,000 members.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: About 668,000 members.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose very first stake (a group of congregations) was organized 1970-1973
prompts.text_original: In the early 1970s the Church organized the first stakes in several lands in Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific. A country or territory whose very first stake of the Church was organized between 1970 and 1973.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies and overviews (Peru, Japan, South Africa, French Polynesia, Chile, South Korea, El Salvador, Philippines)
prompts.note: American Samoa (1969), Tonga (1968) and Denmark (1974) fall just outside. The Philippines' first stake came in May 1973.
prompts.summary: In 1970 the Church organized the first stakes in Peru, Japan and South Africa, Tokyo's being the first in Asia. Tahiti and Santiago, Chile followed in 1972, and in 1973 Seoul, San Salvador and Manila gained the first stakes in South Korea, El Salvador and the Philippines.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: The Tokyo Stake, the first stake in Asia, was organized March 15, 1970, with Kenji Tanaka as president.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: The Santiago Chile Stake, the first in Chile, was organized November 19, 1972.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: The Seoul Korea Stake, the first in mainland Asia, was organized March 8, 1973, with Rhee Ho Nam as president.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: The Lima Stake was organized February 22, 1970, with Roberto Vidal as president.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Elder Ezra Taft Benson organized the Manila Philippines Stake, the first in the country, May 20, 1973, with Augusto A. Lim as president.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: The Transvaal Stake, the first in South Africa, was organized in Johannesburg, March 22, 1970.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: The Tahiti Stake, the first in French Polynesia, was organized at Papeete, May 14, 1972.

answers.name: El Salvador
answers.fact: The San Salvador Stake was created June 3, 1973, with Mario Edmundo Scheel as president.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a city Solomon built, or the homeland of one of his wives or royal allies (not Sheba)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a city Solomon built or fortified, or the homeland of one of his wives or royal allies (Kings and Chronicles; not the queen of Sheba). Trade lands of disputed site, such as Ophir and Tarshish, are not asked.
prompts.note: Jerusalem is scored as Israel, as in the other Bible prompts; Beth-horon the nether is in the West Bank.
prompts.summary: Solomon fortified Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer, built Tadmor and store cities in Hamath, and traded cedar with Hiram of Tyre. He married Pharaoh's daughter and many foreign wives from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Zidon and the Hittites (1 Kgs 3-11; 2 Chr 8-9).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Solomon built Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer (1 Kgs 9:15) and the temple at Jerusalem.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: He married Pharaoh's daughter, who brought Gezer as a dowry (1 Kgs 3:1; 9:16).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Hiram king of Tyre sent cedars of Lebanon for the temple, and Solomon loved women of the Zidonians (1 Kgs 5:1-10; 11:1).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: He loved women of the Moabites, Ammonites and Edomites (1 Kgs 11:1); Naamah the Ammonitess bore Rehoboam (1 Kgs 14:21).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: He built Tadmor in the wilderness and store cities in Hamath (2 Chr 8:3-4).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: He built Beth-horon the nether, now in the West Bank (1 Kgs 9:17).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: He loved Hittite women (1 Kgs 11:1); the Bible Dictionary says the Hittite empire reached into Asia Minor.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Spanish- or Portuguese-speaking South American country where lasting missionary work began from 1956 to 1966
prompts.text_original: After the first South American missions in Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay, missionaries pushed west and north. A Spanish- or Portuguese-speaking South American country where lasting full-time missionary work began between 1956 and 1966.
prompts.summary: Missionary work reached Argentina in 1925, Brazil by 1930, Uruguay in 1947 and Paraguay in 1950. Then came a second wave of lasting work: Chile and Peru in 1956, Bolivia in 1964, Ecuador in 1965, and Colombia and Venezuela in 1966.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Parley P. Pratt's 1851-52 mission was brief; Verle M. Allred and Joseph C. Bentley began lasting work in Santiago, June 1956.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: The first full-time missionaries arrived in Lima, August 1956.

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: J. Vernon Sharp preached briefly in La Paz in 1927; missionaries arrived to stay in La Paz and Cochabamba, November 1964.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Formal preaching began in Bogota in May 1966, with Spencer W. Kimball present.

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: Missionaries from the Andes Mission arrived in Quito, October 1965.

answers.name: Venezuela
answers.fact: Full-time missionaries arrived in Caracas, November 1966.

prompts.display_text: Pin a European country where a current General Authority Seventy served as a young full-time missionary.
prompts.text_original: Many General Authority Seventies serving as of October 2026 were once young full-time missionaries. Pin a European country where one of them served that mission, as named in the Church's official biographies.
prompts.citation: Church leader biographies, General Authority Seventies, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Before their calls as General Authorities, many Seventies served as young missionaries abroad. As of October 2026, their biographies name European missions in England, Scotland, Germany, France, Italy, Switzerland, Portugal, Russia, Finland and the Czech Republic.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: England Manchester, London East and London South; Scotland Edinburgh missions (Elders Phillips, Boom, Hirst, Holland).

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Germany Munich (Elder Holmes) and Germany Hamburg (Elder Cook) missions.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: France Toulouse Mission (Elder Stanfill).

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Switzerland Geneva (Elder Carpenter) and Zurich (Elder Daines) missions.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Elder Brian K. Taylor served in the Spain Seville Mission.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Italy Rome Mission, 1981 to 1983 (Elder De Feo).

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: Portugal Lisbon Mission (Elders Dushku and Teixeira).

answers.name: Finland
answers.fact: Finland Helsinki Mission (Elder Pearson).

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: Russia St. Petersburg Mission (Elder Hathaway).

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: Czech Prague Mission (Elder McConkie).
